title: THE DARK REALITY OF AI'S BLACK MARKETS

beats.vo: This job interview looks normal. But the person on camera isn't who he says he is.

clip.plate: Simon Wijckmans · catches fake job applicants · EMF Camp 2026

beats.vo: Welcome to the grey zone of A.I.
beats.say: Welcome to the grey zone of A I.

beats.vo: Grey, because the tools themselves are legal. A voice cloner reads audiobooks. A face swap finishes a film.
But the very same tools are sold to criminals, in black markets that look like any online shop.

clip.plate: Alexej Hock & Max Bernhard · fraud researchers · 38C3

beats.vo: A shop of shops. By the end, you'll know who sells these tools, who really pays for them, and the one word that beats a cloned voice.
So, the shop. A black market is a website that sells stolen or illegal things. Most hide on the dark web, a part of the internet you can only open with special software.
Inside, it feels like any online store, with product pictures and star ratings. One researcher broke into a scam gang's system, and found this.

clip.plate: Chiao-Lin Yu · hacked scam gangs' websites · 39C3

beats.vo: Even customer support. And what's on the shelves? Stolen card numbers, hacked accounts, even whole identities: a name, a selfie and a photo of an I.D. card.
beats.say: Even customer support. And what's on the shelves? Stolen card numbers, hacked accounts, even whole identities: a name, a selfie and a photo of an I D card.

beats.vo: And lately, a new kind of product: A.I.
beats.say: And lately, a new kind of product: A I.

clip.plate: Chiao-Lin Yu · hacked scam gangs' websites · 39C3

beats.vo: It started with chatbots. In twenty twenty-three, a chatbot called WormGPT went on sale on a hacking forum, for sixty euros a month.
beats.say: It started with chatbots. In twenty twenty-three, a chatbot called Worm G P T went on sale on a hacking forum, for sixty euros a month.

beats.vo: Ask a normal chatbot to write a scam email, and it says no. This one was built to say yes.
Weeks later came FraudGPT, on the chat app Telegram, for two hundred dollars a month.
beats.say: Weeks later came Fraud G P T, on the chat app Telegram, for two hundred dollars a month.

beats.vo: Many of these are just normal chatbots with the safety rules tricked away. That trick has a name: a jailbreak.
Others go further, and cut the refusal right out of the model.

clip.plate: Anykey · on uncensored AI models · Hacker Hotel 2025

beats.vo: A chatbot that never says no. So a scammer who can't write good English now sends perfect emails, in any language, by the thousand.
Chatbots aren't the only thing for rent. Whole phishing kits are rented out like a streaming subscription.
Phishing is a fake message that sends you to a fake login page, to steal your password.
The kit gives you the fake pages, a control panel to watch the victims come in, and a help desk. Here's how one deal works.

clip.plate: Karl Lovink · tracks phishing-kit sellers · Hacker Hotel 2025

beats.vo: The best support you can get. And the newest kits even beat the six-digit code from your phone. The fake page sits in the middle and passes your code to the real site, live.
Then it keeps your session cookie: a small file that tells the site you're already logged in. Your password doesn't matter anymore.

clip.plate: Rik van Duijn & Wesley Neelen · phishing researchers · WHY2025

beats.vo: A fake page in the middle of every login, passing everything on, live.
Some criminals don't even need you to type. An infostealer is a small program hidden inside a free game or a cracked app.
Once it runs, it copies every password saved in your browser, plus your cookies, and sends them away in one file, called a log.

clip.plate: Frank Breedijk · warns hacking victims (DIVD) · WHY2025

beats.vo: Why break in, when you can buy the key? Logs are sold in bulk. When police shut down one market, Genesis, in twenty twenty-three, it held over eighty million stolen logins.
Now the dark part. Hong Kong, twenty twenty-four. An employee joins a video call with his finance chief.
A deepfake is a fake video or voice, made by A.I. to copy a real person.
beats.say: A deepfake is a fake video or voice, made by A I to copy a real person.

beats.vo: Hard to tell apart. And every face on that call was a deepfake. He sent twenty-five million dollars.
Faking a face used to take a film studio. Now it takes a laptop and a few photos from social media.
And a voice is even easier to fake.
Those few seconds are easy to find: a video you posted, or a short call where you only said hello.
Then comes the call. It's your son, crying. There's been an accident, and he needs money now.
It sounds exactly like him. The F.B.I. warned about this very scam in December twenty twenty-four.
beats.say: It sounds exactly like him. The F B I warned about this very scam in December twenty twenty-four.

beats.vo: Now, back to that job interview. The applicant was working for North Korea.
Workers like him use stolen identities, a face swap on camera, and A.I. to write their answers, live.
beats.say: Workers like him use stolen identities, a face swap on camera, and A I to write their answers, live.

beats.vo: In America, one woman kept a room full of company laptops at her home, so the workers looked local. A laptop farm.

clip.plate: Simon Wijckmans · catches fake job applicants · EMF Camp 2026

beats.vo: Her scheme, in Arizona, got jobs at three hundred and nine companies, and made seventeen million dollars. She got eight and a half years in prison.
So, who really cashes in? The sellers. They get paid every month, by every buyer, whether the scam works or not.

clip.plate: Chiao-Lin Yu · inside a scam gang's chat · 39C3

beats.vo: A real company, with sales targets. And the buyers play a numbers game: a million cheap tries, and only a few have to work.

In twenty twenty-five, Americans reported almost twenty-one billion dollars lost to online crime. For the first time, the F.B.I. counted A.I. scams on their own: eight hundred and ninety-three million.

beats.vo: And that's only what people report. Most victims never do. The good news? Defenders use A.I. too.
beats.say: And that's only what people report. Most victims never do. The good news? Defenders use A I too.

beats.vo: So how do you protect yourself? First, slow down. Every one of these scams needs you to hurry.
Second, if a call asks for money, hang up and call back on a number you already know.
Third, pick a secret word with your family. A clone can copy a voice. It can't know your word.
And fourth, never install cracked apps, and turn on passkeys: a login that lives on your phone, so a fake page has nothing to steal.
beats.say: And fourth, never install cracked apps, and turn on pass keys: a login that lives on your phone, so a fake page has nothing to steal.

A.I. didn't invent any of these crimes. It just made them cheap. So the next face on your screen that looks perfectly normal? Normal is exactly what they're selling.
